subject.title: feat(config): add compaction.thinkingLevel to override thinking level during compaction

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a global `agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel` setting when it applies to embedded compaction but is intentionally ignored by native Codex app-server compaction?
rationale: The code can implement either outcome, but choosing whether this asymmetric runtime scope is an acceptable enduring operator contract requires product and ownership intent rather than a mechanical patch repair.

options.title: Approve the scoped setting
options.body: Accept the embedded-only override and native-Codex warning as the documented permanent contract, then rebase and land with focused regression proof.

options.title: Keep inherited thinking only
options.body: Reject the new configuration surface and retain the existing per-session thinking behavior until one model applies consistently across supported compaction runtimes.

options.title: Narrow the product boundary
options.body: Redesign the setting as an explicitly embedded-runtime-owned configuration surface if maintainers want the capability without implying native Codex support.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped setting
recommendation.body: Accept the embedded-only override and native-Codex warning as the documented permanent contract, then rebase and land with focused regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent direct authorship of the integrated compaction and SDK-surface changes makes this the strongest available product-boundary routing signal.
